transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2028-02-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood Product), Liam O'Neill (Ironclad Head of Search), Priya Kapoor (Ironclad ML Engineer), Marcus Reed (Ironclad CTO)
Recording ID: ff-20280212-iron-8932

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking for Ironclad Retail search relevance. Discussed baseline eval, latency vs cost tradeoffs, VPC vs hosted, and next steps for a one-week POC.

Topics:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint and batching
- Reranker endpoint and pairwise scoring
- Console evals & Redwood Optimize recommendations
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, VPC options
- POC approach and success metrics

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Alright, hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE for this account, we also have Ethan our solutions engineer and Maya on product, um, and you all?
[00:07] Liam O'Neill: Hey yes hi Liam, thanks, I'm the head of search at Ironclad Retail, we run discovery and onsite search for our e‑commerce platform.
[00:12] Priya Kapoor: Priya here, ML eng, I own embeddings infra and the offline evals.
[00:16] Marcus Reed: Marcus CTO, quick time check, we have 45 minutes, is that right?
[00:20] Sofia Martinez: Yep 45, great. Goal today: show the hosted API flow for embeddings and the reranker and figure out a POC plan.

[00:35] Ethan Cho: I'll kick off with the live demo — quick note, we'll show the console, the API calls, and a small notebook doing batch embeddings + a rerank call. We also have an Optimize section that gives quantization and batching suggestions, which is handy for cost tuning.

[01:10] Ethan Cho: (screen share) Ok first the embeddings endpoint — you POST your text list, we return dense vectors. We support streaming and async batch jobs for big sets. For 10k SKUs it's common to use our batch job with prefix caching during reindex.
[01:30] Priya Kapoor: Sorry can you clarify prefix caching? we— do you mean KV cache on the model or caching at request layer?
[01:36] Ethan Cho: Good question, it's two levels — KV cache inside the runtime for generation, but for embeddings we do workload-aware caching at the CDN/edge to avoid re-embedding unchanged items. It's in the Optimize tab as "candidate caching".

[02:05] Liam O'Neill: Latency numbers please — our site wants sub 100ms for query + rerank in critical paths.
[02:11] Ethan Cho: On hosted API, typical embed call p50 is 15–25ms for small batches, p95 depends; rerank incurs model latency plus network. Our recommended pattern is: coarse recall with approximate vectors (fast), then call reranker for top 20 results to keep total under your 100–150ms SLO. We can also push the reranker to dedicated capacity for tighter SLAs.
[02:40] Marcus Reed: So dedicated would be reserved GPUs? what's the cost delta roughly?
[02:46] Maya Patel: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p95, cost is higher but unit cost can be lower at scale. We'll include a pricing sheet, but for a pilot hosted is easiest — you can later shift to dedicated if throughput/SLOs require it.

[03:10] Priya Kapoor: For the reranker, are we doing cross-encoder style full-text pairwise or a lightweight scoring function?
[03:16] Ethan Cho: Our rerank endpoint supports both. You can run a small cross-encoder (opt-size models) for higher quality — it's what we demoed — or use a pointwise score with tuned prompt templates for faster throughput. Optimize tab will recommend a quantization profile if you want to run a smaller cross-encoder.

[03:50] (brief audio glitch) 
[04:05] Liam O'Neill: Ok show us an actual request sequence.
[04:11] Ethan Cho: Sure — call 1: POST /v1/embeddings with array of product titles — returns vectors. Call 2: run ANN search (client side) to get top N, then POST to /v1/rerank with the query plus hits — we return ordered list with scores and explanation tokens if you enable structured outputs. I'll paste the curl in chat.
[04:42] Priya Kapoor: Can the rerank output be token‑level explanations? we want to show relevance signals in UI.
[04:49] Ethan Cho: Yes, structured output supports token spans and a short reason string. Note that enabling those increases latency slightly, but it's useful for debugging and UX.

[05:15] Liam O'Neill: We're currently using FAISS + a light ML ranker. We also have Redis for caching. How would Redwood plug in?
[05:22] Sofia Martinez: Most customers keep their vector DB for recall and call Redwood's rerank; you can also use our embeddings and store them where you like. For a fast POC we can run your 10k dataset against our hosted embeddings + reranker and give benchmark numbers.

[06:00] Priya Kapoor: Data residency: can customer data be kept in our VPC? we have compliance for EU data.
[06:06] Ethan Cho: For EU residency and stricter compliance we offer Redwood Private (VPC or on‑prem). Hosted API can be region-locked but if you need isolation we recommend Private. We'll share SOC2 + ISO docs.

[06:35] Marcus Reed: Encryption at rest — KMS support?
[06:38] Maya Patel: Yep KMS/HSM integrations are available for Private and Dedicated, hosted can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping in enterprise plans.

[07:08] (Sofia types link into chat) Link: https://redwood.ai/poc-deck (note: placeholder link)

[07:22] Ethan Cho: Demo note: We'll run a quick live rerank with 6 sample queries on a 500-item subset to show differences between coarse recall only vs recall + rerank.
[07:35] (demo runs; approximate timestamps omitted during screen updates)
[10:10] Ethan Cho: Results: recall-only MRR ~0.61, recall+rerank MRR ~0.82 on that sample — big lift for queries with intent nuance. Priya: these numbers align with your offline eval expectations?
[10:23] Priya Kapoor: They're higher than our internal baseline for similar models, nice. How reproducible is this across product categories with short titles?
[10:31] Ethan Cho: Short titles can be tricky; Optimize suggests using hybrid fields (title + short description + attribute tokens) in embeddings to improve signal. Also reranker prompt templates tuned per vertical help.

[11:00] Liam O'Neill: What's the cost pattern if we rerank top 50 vs top 20?
[11:05] Maya Patel: Roughly linear in rerank calls — top 20 is a good compromise; top 50 doubles compute. Optimize will give estimated per-call token cost for your chosen model.

[11:40] Priya Kapoor: About model versions — can we pin a model and do canary rollouts?
[11:45] Ethan Cho: Yes, the Console supports model pinning and canaries. You can run A/B with traffic split and automatic rollback on quality regression alerts tied to your eval set.

[12:10] Marcus Reed: We'll want audit logs for anything touching PII — do you provide that?
[12:14] Sofia Martinez: Audit logs and request/response tracing are part of enterprise tiers; Private gives full control and long retention. We'll include the retention options in the security packet.

[12:45] (customer side whisper) "we should test mobile latency"
[12:50] Liam O'Neill: Mobile is huge for us, we need a 120ms budget for full roundtrip.
[12:55] Ethan Cho: You can set a policy to route mobile queries to a faster small-model path or lower candidate size; also prefix caching helps for repeat views.

[13:30] Priya Kapoor: How about batch reindexing — do you provide tooling to convert store data and compute embeddings offline?
[13:36] Maya Patel: We have batch import jobs and an SDK; common flow is: compute embeddings with our batch API or an on-prem runner, store in your DB, and use our scoring/rerank endpoints. We'll share a starter notebook.

[14:10] Liam O'Neill: Competitors question — why not just use Pinecone + a Lambda cross-encoder?
[14:15] Sofia Martinez: Pinecone is great for vector storage; Redwood focuses on serving inference (reranking, consistent SLOs, runtime optimizations) and observability. The value is the unified runtime, auto-batching, and Optimize recommendations — fewer moving parts vs a DIY lambda fleet. Also the console has built-in evals so you can track regressions.

[15:00] Priya Kapoor: Any limitations on tokens in rerank input? our product descriptions are long.
[15:05] Ethan Cho: Max combined token payload is around 8k tokens on hosted, we can provide extended limits on Dedicated. For long descriptions we recommend dense embeddings of trimmed fields and optionally include a small context window for reranker.

[15:45] (short pause)
[16:00] Demo: show Optimize tab — recommends quantize int8 for reranker model and batching size 16 for embeddings for lower cost without large quality drop.

[17:10] Priya Kapoor: Quantization — do you do QLoRA or just kernel-level int8?
[17:15] Maya Patel: It's runtime int8 kernels and weight quantization; Optimize gives a recommended profile per model. For Private you can also apply custom quant artifacts.

[18:00] Liam O'Neill: Security again — SSO, SAML, RBAC?
[18:05] Sofia Martinez: Yes SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles in Console. We can demo admin flows in a follow-up.

[19:00] Marcus Reed: Cost — show us a sample estimate for our 10k SKUs, 100k queries/day traffic.
[19:06] Maya Patel: (shares quick back-of-envelope) If you use hosted embeddings + recall in-house + rerank top 20 on 100k q/day, estimated monthly is in the mid‑5 figures, varies by model. We'll send more precise worksheet.

[21:40] Priya Kapoor: For the POC, what would success metrics be?
[21:44] Sofia Martinez: Typically MRR lift on search, CTR lift, and latency SLO adherence. For the pilot we suggest: 5% MRR uplift or 10% CTR improvement, and p95 latency under 200ms for desktop.

[22:10] (customer discussion off mic about internal timeline)

[26:00] Sofia Martinez: Ok to recap next steps — we'll send pricing & security docs, Ethan will share the starter notebook and VPC checklist, Priya will upload sample data and we'll schedule a POC kickoff on 2028-02-20.

[26:30] Liam O'Neill: Sounds good, one question — will you run a baseline run with our data or do we run it?

[26:36] Ethan Cho: We can run an initial baseline if you provide the CSV; otherwise we can give you a self-serve notebook. For speed we'll run baseline on our side if you grant temporary S3 share.

[27:05] Priya Kapoor: I'll get that uploaded by the 17th.

[27:20] Marcus Reed: Any blockers from infra side?
[27:24] Sofia Martinez: Not really — just need the dataset and access choices, we handle the rest.

[27:45] (wrap up) 
[27:50] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and action items. Expect emails from me and Ethan.
